headline.headline: KNICKS BRING NBA FINALS HOME FOR FIRST TIME IN 27 YEARS
headline.deck: New York leads San Antonio 2-0 as Madison Square Garden hosts Game 3 Monday night
headline.body:
For the first time since June 25, 1999, the NBA Finals will be played at Madison Square Garden on Monday night, and Jalen Brunson and the New York Knicks arrive with a commanding 2-0 series lead over Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs. The city that never sleeps has not had a moment like this in a generation, and the Knicks have made certain their fans will see championship basketball in midtown Manhattan before this series is finished.

Brunson, the Knicks' unquestioned leader, kept his focus measured and businesslike on Sunday as New York prepared for the arrival of this historic occasion. The point guard has refused to let the gravity of the moment serve as a distraction, repeating the same message that carried the franchise through the Eastern Conference playoffs: handle each game in sequence, trust the work, let the results speak.

For the Spurs, the deficit is real and the margin for error has evaporated. Wembanyama and San Antonio's coaching staff expressed confidence Sunday that the series is far from over, citing their ability to make adjustments and their belief that the young franchise cornerstone has the talent to will them back into contention. Game 3 tips off Monday at Madison Square Garden, and New York has not felt electricity quite like this since the last millennium.

secondary.headline: MCNABB PLAYS THROUGH STITCHES AS VEGAS TAKES 2-1 SERIES LEAD OVER CAROLINA
secondary.deck: Golden Knights defenseman's battered face a testament to Vegas grit heading into Game 4
secondary.body:
Brayden McNabb skated onto the ice for Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Finals with at least two dozen stitches lacing his face, and the Vegas Golden Knights rewarded his toughness with a victory that put them ahead of the Carolina Hurricanes two games to one. Coach Rod Brind'Amour told reporters Sunday he does not anticipate major changes to his Game 4 lineup after the Hurricanes fell behind in the series, though he declined to confirm specific personnel decisions ahead of the matchup.

Vegas now sits one win closer to another Stanley Cup with Game 4 scheduled for the coming days. The Golden Knights, who finished the regular season at 39-26-17 in the Pacific Division, have shown throughout these playoffs that they are capable of weathering injury and adversity. McNabb's stitched-up visage has already become the defining image of this Finals run, a symbol of the relentless character that has made Vegas a perennial championship contender.

secondary.headline: BRAVES STUN PIRATES WITH THREE-RUN SEVENTH TO CLAIM 3-2 VICTORY
secondary.deck: Atlanta rallies from two runs down against Pittsburgh, scoring all three runs in decisive seventh inning
secondary.body:
The Pittsburgh Pirates carried a 2-0 lead into the seventh inning at Truist Park on Sunday and left Atlanta with a 3-2 defeat, undone by a three-run seventh that turned the game entirely on its head. The Braves had been held scoreless through six innings while Pittsburgh built its advantage on a first-inning run and another in the third. Before a crowd of 37,697, Atlanta exploded for all three of its runs in a single frame to complete the comeback in a game that lasted two hours and 33 minutes.

Pittsburgh threatened nothing in the final two innings and was retired in order to end the contest. Davis, H was replaced by a pinch hitter in the eighth, and Ozuna was lifted for a pinch hitter who doubled in the ninth as the Pirates attempted to extend their at-bats. The loss pushes Pittsburgh further from the division picture while the Braves, playing at home, capitalized on the moment their lineup finally broke through.

secondary.headline: JETS BANK ON VETERAN LEADERSHIP TO REVERSE COURSE IN 2026
secondary.deck: New York adds 44 years of combined experience in offseason bid to end playoff drought
secondary.body:
The New York Jets spent the 2026 offseason accumulating veteran presence in an effort to stop the organizational bleeding, bringing in players whose combined NFL experience totals 44 years. The front office made clear that winning is no longer a distant aspiration but an immediate demand, and the moves reflect a franchise that believes proven leadership in the locker room can accelerate the development of younger contributors and stabilize a roster that has underperformed expectations for several seasons running.

Elsewhere around the league, Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett is expected to report for Arizona's mandatory minicamp this week after a period of uncertainty surrounding his commitment to the team. The Cardinals' quarterback situation had drawn scrutiny heading into the offseason program, and Brissett's arrival at minicamp should provide some clarity to a franchise sorting out its options at the most important position on the field as the 2026 campaign approaches.

column.headline: WEMBANYAMA IS SPECIAL, BUT DOWN 2-0, SAN ANTONIO NEEDS A MIRACLE
column.body:
Victor Wembanyama is unlike anything the NBA has produced in decades, a seven-foot-four force with the skill set of a perimeter scorer and the wingspan of a small aircraft. Nobody disputes that. But talent alone has never won a Finals series from two games down on the road, and the Spurs need more than confidence and press conference bravado if they intend to claw back from a 2-0 deficit against a Knicks team that is playing the best basketball in the Eastern Conference.

Madison Square Garden on a Monday night in June, with New York up two games and the crowd loud enough to rattle windows on Seventh Avenue, is not a forgiving environment for a young team trying to find its footing. San Antonio's belief is admirable, and this column respects a franchise that has won before and knows how to carry itself. But the arithmetic is brutal, the history is against them, and Jalen Brunson is not the type of player who lets a series slip away once he has his hands around its throat.

story.headline: YANKEES UNLOAD IN EIGHTH, ROUT RED SOX 6-1 AT BRONX
story.deck: Five-run eighth inning buries Boston as Bellinger and Jr. go deep
story.body:
NEW YORK — The New York Yankees turned a tense 1-1 game into a rout in the blink of an eighth inning Sunday, erupting for five runs to dispatch the Boston Red Sox, 6-1, before 46,144 fans at Yankee Stadium. The Yankees had managed just a single run through seven innings before blowing the game open, putting the bitter rivalry out of reach in one decisive frame.

Cory Bellinger launched his ninth home run of the season, and Jr. added his eighth, powering the Yankees' attack on a night when both offenses sputtered for long stretches. Doubles from Contreras, Seigler, Grisham, and Caballero kept the lineup moving, while Rosario and Grisham each swiped a bag. Boston's lone run came in the sixth inning, leaving the Red Sox stranded 11 times on base and unable to string anything together against a Yankees staff that kept them off the board the rest of the way.

The loss drops Boston to 27-36, dead last in the AL East, and the Red Sox now head to Tampa Bay to face the first-place Rays, who sit at 37-25 after Miami handed them a 4-1 defeat on Sunday. The Yankees held a weather delay of 20 minutes but were never truly threatened, finishing the job in 2 hours and 37 minutes and tightening their grip on the division race.

story.headline: KING REMEMBERED, FINALS FEVER BUILDS AS NEW YORK BRACES FOR TRUMP, GAME 3
story.deck: Stacey King dies at 59 as the NBA Finals return to Madison Square Garden for first time since 1999.
story.body:
Stacey King, the 6-foot-11 center who won three NBA championships alongside Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen with the Chicago Bulls and later charmed a generation of fans as a color commentator on Bulls broadcasts, died Monday at the age of 59. King, selected sixth overall in the 1989 NBA Draft, was a beloved presence in the Chicago sports landscape long after his playing days ended, known for his thunderous calls and infectious enthusiasm behind the microphone. The NBA community mourned his passing as the league prepared for one of its most anticipated Finals nights in decades.

The circus arrived in full force at Madison Square Garden on Monday, as President Donald Trump's announced attendance at Game 3 of the NBA Finals between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs prompted the NYPD to cancel a planned public watch party due to enhanced security measures. The Garden, hosting its first Finals game since June 25, 1999, when the Knicks fell to the San Antonio Spurs in Game 5 of that series, buzzed with a frantic energy that the city had not felt in more than a quarter century. Jalen Brunson led the Knicks through a calm morning shootaround, insisting the team remained locked in despite the mounting spectacle surrounding the building.

In San Antonio's corner, Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs spoke with measured confidence despite trailing the series two games to none, vowing to steal home-court advantage in New York before the series shifted back to the Frost Bank Center. Meanwhile, the Minnesota Timberwolves offered a brief distraction from Finals mania by unveiling a sweeping rebrand that the franchise described as a fusion of its most recognizable historical elements, featuring updated uniforms, a refreshed logo and redesigned courts intended to honor the team's roots while pushing toward a new era.

story.headline: MCNABB'S STITCHED-UP FACE BECOMES SYMBOL OF VEGAS PUSH FOR ANOTHER CUP
story.deck: Golden Knights carry 2-1 series lead and a warrior's grit into Game 4 against Carolina
story.body:
LAS VEGAS -- Brayden McNabb skated onto the ice for Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Finals with at least two dozen stitches lacing his face together, and the Vegas Golden Knights skated off with a double-overtime victory and a 2-1 series lead over the Carolina Hurricanes. The gruesome image of McNabb absorbing punishment and refusing to yield has galvanized a Vegas locker room that now stands two wins away from hoisting the Stanley Cup, with oddsmakers reinstalling the Golden Knights as favorites to claim the title after the wild extra-session win.

Carolina coach Rod Brind'Amour, whose Hurricanes posted the best record in the Metropolitan Division at 53-22-7, offered no clarity Monday on potential lineup changes heading into Game 4. 'I don't anticipate a lot of changes,' Brind'Amour said, a measured response that masked the urgency facing a team that allowed Vegas to wrestle away home-ice advantage. The Hurricanes, built on relentless forecheck pressure and stingy defensive structure, have the personnel to claw back into this series, but time and margin are both shrinking fast.

Away from the rink, Connor McDavid of the Edmonton Oilers added another chapter to his generational legacy Monday, tying Wayne Gretzky with his fifth Ted Lindsay Award as the NHL's most outstanding player as voted by his peers. The honor underscored McDavid's continued dominance even as the spotlight belongs this week to Las Vegas, where a scarred and resolute McNabb and the Golden Knights prepare to deliver what could be a series-defining blow when the puck drops for Game 4.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026 CAMPAIGN
story.deck: Several franchises are reshaping their rosters this spring with bold moves at the most critical position.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has turned into a full-blown quarterback market this May, with multiple franchises parting ways with veterans and chasing upgrades before training camps open in late July. The Cleveland Browns, still searching for stability under center after years of turbulence, agreed to terms with free agent veteran Sam Darnold on a two-year deal worth $54 million, betting the former Viking can replicate the late-career resurgence he showed in Minnesota. Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders shipped struggling starter Gardner Minshew to the New England Patriots for a conditional third-round pick, clearing the way for second-year man Aidan O'Connell to take full ownership of the starting role in the desert.

The NFL Draft class of 2026 continued to reshape rosters as teams finished evaluating their picks from last month's selection meeting in Green Bay. The Tennessee Titans, who held the first overall pick, used it on Colorado quarterback Shedeur Sanders, and offensive coordinator Tim Kelly wasted no time installing Sanders in a pro-style system built to showcase his pocket precision. Scouts around the league praised the Titans for resisting pressure to reach for a raw dual-threat prospect, calling Sanders the most polished passer to enter the draft since Joe Burrow in 2020.

On the trade front, the Dallas Cowboys sent wide receiver CeeDee Lamb to the Detroit Lions in a stunning blockbuster that sent shockwaves through league circles on Tuesday. Dallas received two first-round picks and young cornerback Terrion Arnold in return, signaling a rebuilding direction under new head coach Mike Zimmer, who took over after the Cowboys dismissed Brian Schottenheimer following a 7-10 finish and a first-round playoff exit. Detroit, already a Super Bowl LX contender after its February title run fell short against the Philadelphia Eagles, views Lamb as the final piece needed to push Jared Goff and the Lions offense over the top in 2026.
